tagline: Colombo's new harbour city, the sheltered Negombo lagoon, the great natural harbour of Trincomalee and the Jaffna island chain.
summary: Sri Lanka's marine-mobility opportunity rings a tropical island whose best water is sheltered rather than open ocean. Colombo, the commercial capital, fronts a working harbour and the new Port City reclamation, with the calm Negombo lagoon and its Dutch canals just north. The east coast holds Trincomalee, one of the world's finest deep natural harbours, and the north the Jaffna lagoon and its island chain — Kayts, Karainagar, Delft — linked today by causeway and slow ferry. The Kalpitiya lagoon on the northwest adds a sheltered dolphin-and-kite coast. The open Indian Ocean swell keeps operation to the lagoons and harbours.
why_marine_mobility: Sri Lanka's usable water is its lagoons and natural harbours — Negombo, Trincomalee, the Jaffna lagoon, Kalpitiya — where the sea is calm and enclosed while the open coast carries ocean swell. Navier's Pioneer II flies these protected hops silent and zero-emission, reconnecting the Jaffna islands and knitting the harbour cities together, while the Quanta-LR's range opens any longer coastal dimension around the island that all-electric craft cannot reach.

demand_signals.label: Colombo harbour & Port City
demand_signals.note: Colombo is the commercial capital and principal port, with the new Port City reclamation adding a large waterfront district beside the working harbour.

demand_signals.label: Jaffna lagoon island chain
demand_signals.note: The northern Jaffna lagoon and its islands — Kayts, Karainagar, Delft — are linked today by causeway and slow ferry across sheltered water, a post-conflict reconnection priority.

demand_signals.label: Trincomalee & Kalpitiya
demand_signals.note: Trincomalee's vast natural harbour on the east and the sheltered Kalpitiya lagoon on the northwest anchor a growing dolphin-, whale- and kite-tourism market on calm water.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling tier on the sheltered Negombo lagoon and Colombo harbour, linking the capital's waterfront on calm, enclosed water.
A faster, cleaner reconnection of the Jaffna lagoon islands — Kayts, Karainagar, Delft — on protected northern water.
Silent wildlife and resort runs on Trincomalee's natural harbour and the Kalpitiya lagoon for the growing east- and northwest-coast tourism market.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The sheltered hops — the Negombo lagoon, Colombo harbour, the Jaffna lagoon islands (~10–20 nm) and the Kalpitiya lagoon — sit within the 70 nm all-electric range on protected water, needing only a berth pedestal.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The lagoons and harbours are Pioneer II territory; any longer coastal dimension — Colombo toward Galle, or around to Trincomalee — would be a Quanta-LR hybrid leg where the range and the more exposed water favour the hybrid drivetrain.

transit_planning: For Sri Lanka's Ports Authority, the Ministry of Ports and Shipping or a Northern Province authority: a clean, zero-emission water tier on the lagoons and natural harbours, reconnecting the Jaffna islands and knitting the harbour cities together, additive to road, causeway and the existing ferries.
competitive_landscape: The Jaffna islands run on slow public ferries and causeways; the Negombo, Trincomalee and Kalpitiya waters carry only informal and tourist boats; and there is no scheduled fast passenger service on any of them. There is no foiling or zero-emission tier on the sheltered water, leaving greenfield room on the lagoons and harbours.
regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under the Sri Lanka Ports Authority and the Merchant Shipping Secretariat, with the lagoons and natural harbours giving protected water that simplifies operation while the open Indian Ocean coast carries swell. Post-conflict reconnection of the Northern Province and the island's tourism-development priorities support a clean lagoon-and-harbour tier.
seasonality: Sri Lanka's two monsoons split the coast: the southwest monsoon (May–September) exposes the west and south while the north and east stay calm, and the northeast monsoon (December–February) reverses it. The sheltered lagoons and natural harbours are largely operable year-round, and a network spanning both coasts can follow the calm side through the year.
